title: Khoresh Narenj
instructions: Cut the duck into serving pieces and season with salt, black pepper, and turmeric.
Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the diced onion until golden.
Add the duck pieces and brown them on all sides for about 10 minutes.
Squeeze the juice from the bitter oranges and set aside, reserving a few strips of the peel.
Add the water to the pot, cover, and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes.
Stir in the bitter orange juice, a few strips of the peel, and the sugar.
Continue simmering uncovered for another 30 minutes until the duck is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Taste and adjust the balance of tartness and sweetness with more sugar or orange juice as needed.
Remove the orange peel strips and serve hot over steamed rice.

title: Chelow Kabab Koobideh
instructions: Grate the onions and squeeze out as much liquid as possible, reserving the pulp.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, ground lamb, grated onion pulp, baking soda, turmeric, salt, and black pepper.
Knead the mixture thoroughly for several minutes until smooth and sticky.
Cover and refrigerate the meat mixture for at least 1 hour to firm up.
Rinse the basmati rice, soak in salted water for 1 hour, then parboil in the water for 6 to 8 minutes and drain.
Steam the parboiled rice with a drizzle of melted butter over low heat for 40 minutes until fluffy.
Divide the meat mixture into portions and mold each firmly onto a flat metal skewer, pressing to remove air pockets.
Preheat a grill to high heat and grill the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning frequently, until fully cooked and lightly charred.
Serve the kabab over the steamed rice with grilled tomatoes.

title: Khoresh Karafs
instructions: Cut the celery stalks into batons and chop the parsley and mint leaves finely.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté the diced onion until golden.
Add the lamb and turmeric, browning the meat on all sides.
Stir in the chopped parsley and mint, cooking for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add the water, season with salt and black pepper, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes.
Add the celery batons and continue simmering for 25 minutes until the celery is tender.
Stir in the lemon juice and simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving hot with steamed rice.

title: Aash-e Jow
instructions: Rinse the barley and lentils, then cook them together in the water over medium heat for 40 minutes until soft.
Finely chop the spinach and parsley.
Sauté one chopped onion in oil until golden, then add the chopped greens and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the sautéed greens to the pot of barley and lentils.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, and season with salt and black pepper.
Remove a ladle of the hot soup and whisk it into the yogurt to temper it, then stir the tempered yogurt back into the pot.
Simmer gently for 5 more minutes without boiling to avoid curdling.
Fry the remaining sliced onion in oil until crispy and golden.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the crispy onions and a drizzle of oil infused with dried mint.

title: Sabzi Polo
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice thoroughly and soak in salted water for 1 hour.
Finely chop the dill, parsley, cilantro, and chives, then combine them in a bowl.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and parboil the drained rice for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
In a clean pot, layer a third of the parboiled rice, then sprinkle with a layer of the chopped herbs.
Continue layering the rice and herbs, finishing with a rice layer on top.
Drizzle melted butter over the top and cover the pot with a towel-wrapped lid.
Steam on low heat for 40 to 45 minutes until the rice is fully cooked and a golden crust forms on the bottom.
Gently fluff and mix the rice and herbs together before transferring to a serving platter.
Serve hot, traditionally alongside fried fish or lamb.

title: Naan-e Sangak
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, instant yeast, and salt.
Gradually add the warm water, mixing and kneading into a soft, elastic dough for about 12 minutes.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 2 hours until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to its highest setting with a baking stone or heavy tray inside.
Divide the dough into portions and stretch each into a long, thin rectangle directly on a floured surface.
Transfer each stretched piece of dough onto the hot baking stone.
Sprinkle the surface with sesame seeds and poppy seeds, pressing them lightly into the dough.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the bread puffs up and develops a deep golden, blistered crust.
Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before tearing and serving.

title: Kotlet
instructions: Boil the potatoes until fully tender, then peel and mash them in a bowl.
Grate the onion and add it to the mashed potatoes along with the ground beef.
Add the eggs, breadcrumbs, turmeric, salt, and black pepper to the mixture.
Knead everything together thoroughly until well combined and smooth.
Shape the mixture into small oval patties with your hands.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties in batches for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain the cooked patties on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Serve warm with bread, herbs, and pickles.

title: Shirin Polo
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice and soak in salted water for 1 hour, then drain.
Cut the orange peel into thin strips and boil in water for 5 minutes to remove bitterness, then drain and repeat once more.
Bloom the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot water.
In a small pan, combine the blanched orange peel, sugar, and a splash of water, and simmer for 10 minutes until syrupy.
Stir in the slivered almonds and pistachios to the orange peel syrup and set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and parboil the drained rice for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
Layer the parboiled rice in a pot with the orange peel and nut mixture, finishing with a rice layer.
Drizzle with melted butter, cover with a towel-wrapped lid, and steam on low heat for 40 minutes.
Mix a portion of the rice with the bloomed saffron water and use it to garnish the platter before serving.

title: Khorak-e Morgh
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and sauté the diced onion until golden.
Add the chicken drumsticks and turmeric, browning them on all sides.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes to deepen the flavor.
Peel and cut the potatoes and carrots into large chunks and add them to the pot.
Pour in the water, season with salt and black pepper, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes until the chicken and vegetables are tender.
Uncover and simmer for 10 more minutes to thicken the sauce slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed before serving hot with bread or rice.

title: Nargesi
instructions: Wash the spinach thoroughly and roughly chop it.
Heat the oil in a large skillet and sauté the diced onion until golden.
Add the turmeric and chopped spinach to the skillet, stirring to combine.
Cook the spinach over medium heat for 10 minutes until wilted and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Make small wells in the spinach mixture and crack an egg into each well.
Cover the skillet and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the eggs are set to your liking.
Serve hot directly from the skillet with fresh bread.

title: Khoresh Rivas
instructions: Cut the rhubarb into short batons and set aside.
Finely chop the parsley and mint leaves.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté the diced onion until golden.
Add the lamb and turmeric, browning the meat on all sides.
Stir in the chopped parsley and mint, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add the water, season with salt and black pepper, and simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Add the rhubarb batons and sugar, and simmer for 20 more minutes until the rhubarb is soft but not disintegrated.
Taste and adjust the sweet-tart balance with more sugar if needed.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Havij Polo
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice and soak in salted water for 1 hour, then drain.
Cut the carrots into thin matchsticks.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the diced onion until golden, then add the chicken thighs and brown on both sides.
Season the chicken with salt and black pepper, add a splash of water, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until cooked through.
In a separate pan, sauté the carrot matchsticks with sugar for 10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized, then stir in the raisins.
Bloom the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and parboil the drained rice for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
Layer the parboiled rice with the sweet carrot mixture in a pot, finishing with a rice layer, then drizzle with the bloomed saffron water.
Cover with a towel-wrapped lid and steam on low heat for 40 minutes, then serve with the cooked chicken.

title: Ash-e Mast
instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it in the water over medium heat for 20 minutes until tender.
Finely chop the spinach and one onion, then sauté the onion in oil until golden and add the spinach, cooking for 8 minutes.
Stir the sautéed spinach mixture into the pot of cooked rice.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then season with salt and black pepper.
Remove a ladle of the hot soup and whisk it into the yogurt to temper it, then stir the tempered yogurt back into the pot.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes without letting the soup boil to avoid curdling.
Fry the remaining sliced onion in oil until crispy and golden.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with crispy onions and a drizzle of oil infused with dried mint.

title: Morgh-e Torsh
instructions: Grind the walnuts finely in a food processor.
Finely chop the cilantro and parsley.
Heat oil in a pot and sauté the diced onion and minced garlic until golden.
Add the chicken thighs and turmeric, browning them on both sides.
Stir in the ground walnuts, chopped herbs, and water, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the pomegranate paste, salt, and black pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 20 more minutes until the sauce thickens and turns a deep color.
Taste and balance the tartness with more pomegranate paste if needed, then serve hot with rice.

title: Koofteh Tabrizi
instructions: Rinse the rice and split peas, then cook them together in water until soft, about 20 minutes, and drain.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, cooked rice and split peas, grated onion, raw eggs, turmeric, salt, and black pepper.
Knead the mixture thoroughly until smooth and well combined.
Divide the mixture into large portions and flatten each into a disc in your palm.
Place a few prunes and a wedge of hard boiled egg in the center of each disc, then fold the meat around the filling to form a large ball.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté the second chopped onion until golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and water, bringing the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Carefully lower the meatballs into the simmering sauce, cover, and cook for 60 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve the meatballs whole in a bowl with the sauce spooned over the top.

title: Shami Lapeh
instructions: Rinse the split peas and cook them in the water until very soft, about 25 minutes, then drain well.
Mash the cooked split peas into a smooth paste.
In a large bowl, combine the mashed split peas, ground beef, grated onion, turmeric, cinnamon, salt, and black pepper.
Add the eggs and knead everything together until the mixture is smooth and holds together well.
Shape the mixture into small oval patties with your hands.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with bread and fresh herbs.

title: Torshi Bademjan
instructions: Peel the eggplants and cut them into thick slices.
Salt the eggplant slices and let them sit for 20 minutes to draw out bitterness, then rinse and pat dry.
Boil the eggplant slices in salted water for 5 minutes until just softened, then drain thoroughly.
Mince the garlic and combine it with the dried mint, salt, and black pepper.
Layer the boiled eggplant slices in a clean sterilized jar, sprinkling the garlic and mint mixture between each layer.
Pour the white vinegar over the layered eggplant until fully submerged.
Seal the jar tightly and store in a cool, dark place for at least one week before serving.
Serve chilled as a tangy side with rice or bread.

title: Masghati
instructions: In a saucepan, whisk the rice flour with the water until completely smooth and lump-free.
Add the sugar and cardamom to the saucepan and place over medium heat.
Cook the mixture, stirring constantly, until it begins to thicken.
Gradually stream in the vegetable oil while continuing to stir vigorously.
Continue cooking for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture becomes glossy and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Stir in the rose water during the final minute of cooking.
Pour the mixture into a greased shallow dish and smooth the top with a spatula.
Sprinkle the slivered pistachios evenly over the surface.
Let the mixture cool completely at room temperature, then chill until firm before slicing into diamonds.

title: Kachi
instructions: Bloom the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water.
Combine the sugar and the remaining water in a small saucepan and bring to a boil to make a syrup, then set aside.
Heat the oil in a separate pan over medium heat.
Add the flour to the hot oil and stir constantly to avoid lumps or burning.
Toast the flour for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring continuously, until it turns golden and fragrant.
Slowly pour the sugar syrup into the toasted flour while whisking vigorously to prevent clumping.
Stir in the bloomed saffron water and continue cooking for 5 minutes until smooth and thickened.
Pour into serving bowls and sprinkle with cinnamon before serving warm.

title: Lavashak
instructions: Wash the plums thoroughly and remove the pits.
Blend the pitted plums in a food processor until completely smooth.
Pour the puree into a saucepan and add the sugar and a pinch of salt.
Cook the puree over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until slightly thickened.
Line a large flat baking sheet with parchment paper and pour the puree onto it, spreading it into a thin, even layer.
Place the sheet in a very low oven or in direct sun for 6 to 8 hours until the puree is fully dried and no longer tacky.
Once dried, peel the fruit leather away from the parchment paper.
Cut or roll the fruit leather into strips for serving or storage.

title: Sekanjabin
instructions: Combine the sugar and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar fully dissolves.
Reduce the heat and simmer the syrup for 10 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Stir in the white vinegar and continue simmering for 5 more minutes.
Add the fresh mint leaves to the syrup and let them steep for 5 minutes.
Remove the syrup from heat and let it cool completely, then strain out the mint leaves.
Transfer the syrup to a clean bottle and refrigerate until ready to serve.
To serve, dilute a few tablespoons of the syrup with cold water in a glass.
Peel and slice the cucumbers into sticks and serve alongside the drink for dipping.

title: Morasa Polo
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice and soak in salted water for 1 hour, then drain.
Boil the chicken breast with the sliced onion, salt, and black pepper until fully cooked, then shred the meat.
Cut the orange peel into thin strips and boil twice in fresh water to remove bitterness, then drain.
In a small pan, combine the orange peel, sugar, and a splash of water and simmer for 10 minutes until syrupy, then stir in the almonds, pistachios, and barberries.
Bloom the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot water.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and parboil the drained rice for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
Layer the parboiled rice with the shredded chicken and half of the nut and barberry mixture, finishing with a rice layer.
Drizzle melted butter and half of the bloomed saffron water over the top, cover with a towel-wrapped lid, and steam on low heat for 40 minutes.
Transfer to a serving platter and garnish with the remaining nut and barberry mixture and saffron rice before serving.

title: Kufteh Berenji
instructions: Rinse the rice and split peas, then cook them together in water until soft, about 20 minutes, and drain.
Finely chop the fresh herbs and grate one onion.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, cooked rice and split peas, grated onion, chopped herbs, turmeric, salt, and black pepper.
Knead the mixture thoroughly until smooth, then shape into large round balls.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté the remaining chopped onion until golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and water, bringing the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Carefully lower the meatballs into the simmering broth, cover, and cook for 60 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve the meatballs hot in bowls with the broth spooned over the top and fresh bread on the side.

title: Panir-o-Sabzi
instructions: Arrange the fresh basil, mint leaves, and tarragon on a serving platter.
Slice the radishes thinly and add them to the platter.
Place the feta cheese in the center of the platter.
Scatter the walnuts around the cheese.
Warm the flatbread briefly if desired.
Serve immediately, allowing everyone to wrap the cheese, herbs, radish, and walnuts in pieces of the flatbread.

title: Zoolbia
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together the flour, yogurt, and instant yeast until a smooth, thick batter forms.
Cover the batter and let it rest in a warm place for 1 hour until slightly bubbly.
Meanwhile, combine the sugar and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil to make a syrup.
Bloom the saffron in a spoonful of hot water and stir it into the syrup along with the rose water, then simmer for 10 minutes and set aside warm.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan to medium-high heat.
Transfer the batter into a piping bag or squeeze bottle.
Pipe the batter into the hot oil in overlapping pretzel-like shapes, frying for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Remove the fried shapes with a slotted spoon and immediately dip them into the warm syrup for a few seconds.
Let the excess syrup drain off before arranging on a platter and serving.
